mg_south_gate.name: Marrowgate, South Gate
mg_south_gate.desc: A gatehouse of black stone at the top of the pass, the Regent's stag cut over the arch. Guards in gray count everyone in. Below, the Lower Town falls away in slate roofs; above it all, the palace, pale as a tooth.
mg_south_gate.brief: The south gate. Guards in gray.
onEnterOnce: The guards see the Regent's seal on your writ and step back a pace. One of them will not meet your eye.
The pilgrim stair lets out behind the guards' backs. Nobody has watched it in a hundred years.
The guards look you over, decide you are nobody, and wave you through with the carters.

mg_lower_town.name: The Lower Town
mg_lower_town.desc: A market square that climbs, stalls on the steps, the smell of tallow and wet wool. The gray is here too, thin as breath on a window; it comes up the drains at night. The Hanged Man east, the Chapel of Ash west, the Regent's Way north, the warrens down.
mg_lower_town.brief: The market steps. Gray on the drains.

variants.brief: The market steps. The drains have stopped breathing.
The market steps. The drains have gone quiet at last.

actions.label: listen to the market talk
fx: Three things everyone says: the Regent burns the dead now, by decree. The Ironbound have a hall on the Regent's Way. And there is something under the palace that the guards will not go down to, not for double pay.

mg_hanged_man.name: The Hanged Man
mg_hanged_man.desc: A tavern named for its sign and for the square outside. Sawdust, a good fire, and a corner table where a small neat man in a Free Company coat is dealing cards to nobody. The market steps lie west.

actions.label: take a room and sleep
fx: You sleep with your boots on and wake steadier.

mg_market.name: The Upper Market
mg_market.desc: Better stalls under awnings: an armourer, a herb-wife, a cutler with Marrowgate steel. Prices are in the Regent's coin and so are the sellers. The market steps lie down.

actions.label: buy the Marrowgate sword (12 gold)
fx: The cutler wraps it in oiled cloth without asking what you want it for.

actions.label: buy the riveted mail (15 gold)
fx: Heavier than it looks, and it looks heavy. It rides in your pack and turns blows from there.

actions.label: buy a bundle of herbs (3 gold)
fx: The herb-wife ties the bundle with gray thread. 'Everything's gray thread now,' she says.

mg_chapel_of_ash.name: The Chapel of Ash
mg_chapel_of_ash.desc: The Gray Church's house in the capital, and a poor one: whitewash over old soot, a font full of ash instead of water. Mother Ysme keeps it with two novices and no illusions. The market steps lie east.

down.lockedMsg: A trapdoor under the font, bolted. Mother Ysme would have to tell you where it goes.
down.hint: ask Mother Ysme about the pilgrims' door

mg_regents_way.name: The Regent's Way
mg_regents_way.desc: A straight avenue climbing to the palace between houses too grand to have windows at street level. The Watch House stands east with its shutters open; the Ironbound's hall stands west with its doors shut and a brazier burning in daylight.

mg_watch_house.name: The Watch House
mg_watch_house.desc: Racks of pikes, a map of the Reach with pins in it, and Lord Marshal Tarn at a desk too small for him. The Watch in Marrowgate answers to the Regent. The Marshal answers to the Watch, and does not always like it.
mg_watch_house.brief: Pikes and a map with pins.

actions.label: argue her oath before Tarn (will)
fx: Tarn hears you out, arms crossed. 'The Church's oath covers rites for the dead, not the living,' he says, 'but I've a hearing to hold, and better things to hold it over.' He signs her release himself.
Tarn hears you out and is not moved. 'Fine words,' he says. 'Bring me better ones.'

actions.label: hand Quill's coin to the Watch
fx: Tarn turns the purse over once, reads the Company mark, and doesn't ask how you came by it. 'This buys you nothing,' he says, 'but it costs you nothing either, with me.'

mg_ironbound_hall.name: The Ironbound Hall
mg_ironbound_hall.desc: A hall built like a furnace, all iron doors and drafts. Casks of lamp-oil stand in ranks along the wall. The Preceptor-General stands at a lectern reading the roll of the burned, and does not stop when you come in.
mg_ironbound_hall.brief: Iron doors, ranked casks of oil.

actions.label: search the ranked casks (wits)
fx: One cask sits half a hand's-width out of true with the rest. Behind it, folded flat: a burn-order for Tanners' Row, signed and dated, with no hearing number where a hearing number should be.
The casks are ranked too well to hide anything from a glance. The Preceptor keeps reading and does not stop.

mg_palace_gate.name: The Palace Gate
mg_palace_gate.desc: Bronze doors under the stag, a guard captain in enamelled gray, and a smaller servants' door in the wall to one side where a boy carries out ash in buckets. Nobody goes through the bronze without the Regent's word.

north.lockedMsg: The captain does not move. 'The Regent's word, or the Marshal's, or turn around.'
north.hint: the writ, the Marshal's escort, the servants' door, or force

actions.label: show the Regent's writ
fx: The captain reads the writ twice and hands it back with both hands. The bronze doors open for you.

actions.label: present the Marshal's token
fx: The captain looks at the Marshal's token, then at the Watch House, and decides he did not see you.

actions.label: slip through the servants' door (grace)
fx: You take the boy's empty bucket and walk in behind him. Nobody looks at the ash-carriers.
The captain's eye finds you before the door does. You walk on as if you meant to.

mg_palace_court.name: The Palace Court
mg_palace_court.desc: A courtyard of white stone kept scrubbed by people who are never seen doing it. Stairs climb north to the Regent's chambers; a colonnade east leads to the Hall of Ledgers; a barred stair in the corner goes down, and nobody stands near it.

down.lockedMsg: The stair is barred with iron and a lock the size of a fist. The archivist keeps the key; or the lock keeps nothing against a strong enough shoulder.

actions.label: break the stair's bar — fail costs 1hp
fx: The bar gives with a crack that turns every head in the court. Nobody comes.
The bar holds and your shoulder does not.

mg_hall_of_ledgers.name: The Hall of Ledgers
mg_hall_of_ledgers.desc: Four hundred years of the Reach in bound calfskin, floor to vault. Archivist Penn moves among the shelves with a candle he never lets near them. The oldest shelf is chained.
mg_hall_of_ledgers.brief: Shelves to the vault. The chained shelf.

actions.label: find the founding ledger (wits)
fx: The chained shelf is a shelf like the others once you know which chain is only for show. The founding ledger: the first Reeve's own account of the crown, and the names of his line — one of them Vell's.
The chained shelf is a shelf like the others once you know which chain is only for show. The founding ledger: the first Reeve's own account of the crown, in his own hand.
Every shelf looks chained when you are looking for the one that is. Penn watches you look.

actions.label: pick the chain's lock (grace)
fx: The chain drops. The founding ledger: the first Reeve's own account of the crown, and the names of his line — one of them Vell's.
The chain drops. The founding ledger: the first Reeve's own account of the crown, in his own hand.
The lock is older than your fingers know. Penn coughs.

actions.label: search the hearing rolls (wits)
fx: Properly filed, and properly wrong: a burn-order for Tanners' Row with a hearing number that traces to a hearing that was never held. Someone wanted this findable, eventually, by someone patient.
The rolls for that week are thick with names and thin with sense. Penn watches you turn pages and says nothing.

mg_regents_chamber.name: The Regent's Chambers
mg_regents_chamber.desc: A long room with one chair in it and a window that looks down on the whole Reach. Regent Ysolde Ashreeve stands at the window rather than sit. The stag is worked into everything, even the floor.

mg_pilgrims_door.name: The Pilgrims' Door
mg_pilgrims_door.desc: A stair under the chapel font, worn to a trough by knees. Keeper-knots are cut into the wall every ten steps, the same as the Vale's. It lets out below into standing water.

mg_undercity_stair.name: The Barred Stair
mg_undercity_stair.desc: Steps down under the palace, iron-shod, the gray thickening with every turn until your light is a lamp in fog. Someone has scratched a raised hand into the wall at the bottom.

mg_cistern.name: The Undercity Cistern
mg_cistern.desc: A vault of black water under the whole city, pillars marching off into the dark. Three ways in meet here: the barred stair above, the pilgrims' door, and a smugglers' cut from the warrens. The gray pours north along the water like a river in a river.
mg_cistern.brief: Black water, marching pillars. The gray runs north.
onEnterOnce: Whatever is under Marrowgate, the water knows where it is.

mg_smugglers_cut.name: The Smugglers' Cut
mg_smugglers_cut.desc: A tunnel hacked through the cistern wall by people who did not want to pay the gate. Barrels, a lantern, a Free Company mark chalked on the stone. It climbs to the warrens.

mg_free_den.name: Quill's Den
mg_free_den.desc: A cellar under the warrens with too many exits and a card table. Whoever runs it is not here; whoever is here is watching you. A trap in the floor is chalked with the Free Company's mark.
mg_free_den.brief: The cellar with too many exits.

down.lockedMsg: The trap is bolted from beneath. Quill, at the Hanged Man, would know the knock.
down.hint: ask Quill at the Hanged Man about the cut

mg_old_crypts.name: The Old Crypts
mg_old_crypts.desc: The crypts of the kings before the Reeves, robbed to the bone. A shape in gray mail stands where the gray runs thickest — the first Reeve's honour guard, four hundred years at his post, and it lunges the moment it hears a living step.

north.lockedMsg: The honour guard bars the way north. Kill it, slip past it, or turn back.
north.hint: kill it, or slip past it (grace)

variants.desc: The crypts of the kings before the Reeves, robbed to the bone. Gray mail lies in a heap where the guard stood. The way north is open.
variants.brief: Robbed crypts. The guard is down.

actions.label: slip past the guard — fail costs 2hp
fx: You wait for its swing and go under it. The passage north is yours.
It is faster than four hundred years should allow.

mg_first_reeves_tomb.name: The First Reeve's Tomb
mg_first_reeves_tomb.desc: A tomb built for a king by a man who knew he was not one. The stag on the lid is the Hollow King's stag with a bar through it. A shade sits on the lid with its head in its hands, and it is the gray's own source: it comes off him like smoke.
mg_first_reeves_tomb.brief: The barred stag. The shade on the lid.

variants.brief: The barred stag. The shade sits straighter now.

mg_hollow_throne.name: The Hollow Throne
mg_hollow_throne.desc: A throne room under the throne room: the true seat of the Reach, cut from one gray stone and empty at the heart, where a crown was meant to sit and never did. The gray comes up out of that hollow. Everything that grieves in the Reach is fed from here.
mg_hollow_throne.brief: The gray stone seat, hollow at the heart.
onEnterOnce: Footsteps on the stair behind you: Regent Ysolde Ashreeve, alone, with a lamp. 'So,' she says. 'Someone finally came down.'

actions.label: weigh the doors of the seat
fx: Fill it: three holds rested, the Vale's king at rest, the Reeve's confession. Burn it: Ironbound oil. Sit in it: the Vale's crown. Read the ledger aloud: the Watch, Church or Companies must trust you.

actions.label: speak the Great Rite over the seat
fx: You speak the verses of three holds over the hollow seat, and the first Reeve's confession after them, and the stone fills — not with a crown, with quiet. The gray goes out of the water, the drains, the fields of nine holds, like a breath let go. The Reach sleeps.

actions.label: burn the throne with the Ironbound oil
fx: You break the casks over the seat and put the torch to it. The gray burns like fat. When it is done there is nothing under Marrowgate to grieve, and nothing anywhere in the Reach that remembers its dead. The living call that peace, and mostly mean it.

actions.label: read the ledger aloud to the Marshal
fx: You read the first Reeve's own hand aloud, and behind the Regent, Lord Marshal Tarn's men come down the stair with their pikes reversed. The House of Ashreeve ends without a blow, on a lie read out in a cellar. The Watch keeps the Reach until a better answer comes.

actions.label: read the ledger aloud to the Mother
fx: You read the first Reeve's own hand aloud, and Mother Ysme's novices carry the words up the pilgrims' stair to the Lower Town before the Regent has stopped shaking. By morning the city knows what it was founded on. The House of Ashreeve leaves by the north road, unescorted.

actions.label: read the ledger aloud to the Companies
fx: You read the first Reeve's own hand aloud, and Quill's people come out of the smugglers' cut with knives and a grin. The Regent leaves Marrowgate in a barrel-cart, alive, which was the bargain. The Free Companies hold the palace for a season and then, to everyone's surprise, hold an election.

actions.label: sit the throne, wearing the Vale's crown
fx: You set the Hollow King's crown on your own head and sit. The stone takes your weight like it has waited for exactly you. The gray thins across the Reach, and settles behind your eyes, and does not leave either place. You are Regent by dawn. Nobody argues.

actions.label: sit the throne, wearing the Vale's crown
fx: You set the Hollow King's crown on your own head and sit. Vell watches you do it and says nothing at all, which is the worst thing Vell has ever said. The gray thins across the Reach, and settles behind your eyes. You are Regent by dawn.

actions.label: sit the throne, wearing the Vale's crown
fx: You lift the crown toward your head and Vell's hand closes on it first. 'It was always mine,' Vell says, and sits, and the stone takes the exile's weight like it has waited four hundred years for exactly this. The gray thins across the Reach and settles behind Vell's eyes. You are shown the north road.

actions.label: (no dawn) kneel to the hollow seat
fx: You go down on one knee before the empty stone and feel the gray notice you. This is the one door here that does not open back. Kneel again to go through it.

actions.label: (no dawn) finish kneeling
fx: You kneel, and the hollow at the heart of the stone fills with you. The gray has a source with a face now. Across the Reach the dead sit up, all of them, and wait to be told what to grieve. There is no dawn.

descs: Alleys stacked on alleys, washing strung across the gap of sky.

scenes.name: Tallow Court
scenes.desc: A court of candle-makers, every sill greasy, the air thick enough to chew. Someone has scratched a raised hand beside a cellar door.

scenes.name: The Ropewalk
scenes.desc: A long shed open at both ends where two old women walk backward twisting hemp, and have done since before the Regent's mother.

scenes.name: Bell-Founders' Lane
scenes.desc: Cracked bell-moulds used as planters, nothing growing in them. A bell hangs at the lane's end that nobody rings; the gray beads on it like sweat.

scenes.name: The Old Shambles
scenes.desc: Butchers' hooks with nothing on them and a gutter that still runs red on wet days out of habit.

scenes.name: Gray Steps
scenes.desc: A stair between houses so narrow you climb it sideways. Chalked on the risers, the Free Company's mark and an arrow pointing down.

scenes.name: Dyers' Yard
scenes.desc: Vats of dead colour and hands stained to the elbow. Everyone here knows which vat the gray came up in first.

scenes.name: Saint's Alley
scenes.desc: A niche with a stone saint whose face has been rubbed off by centuries of thumbs. Fresh candle-stubs at its feet: someone still asks.

links.landmark: a cellar with the Company's mark

spots.name: The Warrens' Mouth
spots.desc: Where the market steps give up and become alleys. Washing overhead, a beggar in a niche who watches the drains instead of the passers-by, and the smell of the undercity coming up through a grating.
spots.brief: The alleys begin. The beggar's niche.

spots.name: Cutpurse Corner
spots.desc: A dead end that is not: a gap behind a rain-barrel lets a thin person through. Children's chalk games on the flags, and a knife-scratch tally on the wall that is not a game.
onEnterOnce: Two coins in the chalk circle, left as a dare. You take the dare.

onEnter: A boy with a knife and a man's eyes steps out of the washing.

fx: Bitter. The gray thread you spit out.

mg_founding_ledger.name: the founding ledger
mg_founding_ledger.hint: the first Reeve's own account of the crown — read it

fx: 'I took it from his brow while he slept his last sleep, and I called it inheritance, and the vale ate that winter. Let whoever reads this judge me. I could not.' Signed with the stag, and a bar through it.

mg_regent.name: Regent Ysolde
mg_regent.desc: Fifty, gray-eyed, a woman who has read every ledger in the hall and burned none of them.
onDeath: The Regent dies with the stag under her. The Watch comes running and finds you standing over the House of Ashreeve; what they do next depends on who you have been to them. The Reach has no Regent by morning, and the gray does not care either way.

topics.label: why the gray is treason
topics.say: Because grief that will not end is a rebellion against the living. I have fields going gray from here to the sea. I can burn what grieves, or I can hold rites for it and hope. I chose the one I can command.

topics.label: oil to burn the Hollow Throne
topics.say: You know what is under this palace, then. Good. Burn it for me and you will have a title, a hall, and my gratitude, which is worth more than the title. Take the oil from the Preceptor-General; I will send word.

topics.label: refuse to burn anything for her
topics.say: Then we understand each other, at least. The stair is barred and the archivist is loyal. Go home. Whatever is under this palace has waited four hundred years; it can wait past you.

topics.label: the founding ledger (will)
topics.say: You set the first Reeve's own hand on the table between you and say nothing.
fx: She reads it standing. When she looks up she is older. 'I knew,' she says. 'I have always known. I did not know he wrote it down.'
She does not look at it. 'Every house is founded on something. Mine is founded on a winter with no grain. Take that book back to the shelf.'

topics.label: what you did in the Vale
topics.say: My herald told me. The Hollow King was my ancestor's father, did you know? Every Ashreeve does. We are taught it with our letters, and taught never to say it.
fx: 'You rested him,' she says. 'I would not have. Perhaps that is the whole of the difference between us.'
'You cut him down,' she says. 'Good. That, at least, I understand.'
'You left him grieving,' she says, 'with his crown in your pack. You and I are more alike than I would like.'

topics.label: what she makes of the burned holds
topics.say: Word of every hollow put to the torch reaches me before the smoke clears. One debt fewer on my ledger. I approve of debts paid, however they are paid.

topics.label: what she makes of the rested holds
topics.say: Verses and rites, where fire would have been quicker and cheaper. Slower mercy, I call it, most nights, and mean it as an insult. Not all of them.

topics.label: Hollowbrook's map, Gullhaven's watch
topics.say: A surveyor's map out of Hollowbrook, a tip-off from Gullhaven's watch-house. Small loyalties, but I read every one. Not every hold has forgotten whose Reach this is.

topics.label: the burn-order from Tanners' Row
topics.say: You set the burn-order on the table between you and let her read whose hand signed it.
fx: She reads it twice, then folds it away in a drawer that locks. 'Thank you,' she says, and means the drawer, not the truth in it.

topics.label: what became of the Tanners' Row proof
topics.say: Word of the Tanners' Row order reaches me eventually. Everything does.
fx: 'Tarn came to me already knowing,' she says. 'I'll say this for the Marshal: he didn't gloat.'
'Free Company gossip, this time.' She almost smiles. 'I find I mind less than I once would have.'

topics.label: leave the Regent to her window
topics.say: Mind the stair. Everyone who goes down it comes up changed, or does not come up.

mg_marshal.name: Lord Marshal Tarn
mg_marshal.desc: Too big for his desk and his orders both.

topics.label: the Watch in Marrowgate
topics.say: We keep the gate, the Way, and the peace. We do not keep the undercity. The Regent's writ says burn; the Watch's oath says guard. I am trying to do both, and doing neither.

topics.label: get me into the palace
topics.say: The Watch owes you, by every report from the holds. Take my token to the gate captain. If anyone asks, I never met you, and I shall mean it.

topics.label: get me into the palace
topics.say: On whose word? The Watch in the holds has not sent me your name with anything good attached to it. Earn that, and ask again.

topics.label: the Watch's founding
topics.say: Highward sent word. The oath-stone rests. Four hundred years we guarded a road for a thief and called it honour; you gave us the truth and we are still standing. That is worth something. It is worth the palace gate.
fx: He puts his token in your hand.

topics.label: the Watch's good work in the holds
topics.say: A beacon lit on Wardmoor's moor after ten dark years. A tip that shut down smugglers at Gullhaven. A rider at Coldpass who told me true instead of easy. Good work finds me eventually.

topics.label: the record stolen from Highward
topics.say: A record lifted clean off a sealed shelf at Highward, and you were standing closer to it than most. That is not a debt the Watch forgets easily.

topics.label: who ordered Tanners' Row burned
topics.say: Dead pulled from Tanners' Row and burned inside a day, no hearing, no name on the order I can find. Someone signed for that fire. I want to know who.

topics.label: show him the burn-order
topics.say: You put the burn-order flat on his desk, over the map with all its pins.
fx: He reads it through, and doesn't look up for a while. 'The Preceptor,' he says at last. 'Not the Regent. I needed to hear that, more than I wanted to.' He presses a blade of his own making into your hand.

topics.label: the novice from the cells
topics.say: That novice of Mother Ysme's — word of her reached my desk too.
fx: 'Paid square,' he says. 'I've no complaint with coin that settles a debt honest.'
'You argued her free. I still think the Church's oath is a loophole wide enough to drive a cart through. You drove one through it well.'
'My gaoler still won't say how she got out. I have my suspicions. I am choosing, for now, not to act on them.'
'Left her to it, did you. The cells don't forget who walks past them.'

topics.label: leave the Marshal to his map
topics.say: Keep to the Way after dark.

mg_preceptor.name: Preceptor-General Hald
mg_preceptor.desc: Burn-scarred hands and a voice like a closing door.

topics.label: the roll of the burned
topics.say: Every hollow we have put to the fire, and every name in it. Grief has a weight; fire has none. Read it if you like. It gets shorter every year, and the gray does not.

topics.label: oil for the Hollow Throne
topics.say: You know what is down there, then.
fx: He reads your writ and rolls a cask to your feet himself. 'Finish it,' he says. 'Nobody else has had the stomach.'
'The chapterhouse vouches for you,' he says, and rolls a cask to your feet. 'Finish it.'
'The Ironbound do not arm strangers,' he says. 'Bring me the Regent's writ, or two burned hollows to your name, and we will speak.'

topics.label: the Hundred, at Cinderhall
topics.say: Aldous was Preceptor at Cinderhall before he was anything. If he signed off on rotten timber, that is on him, not on the fire. The fire has never lied to anyone.

topics.label: which hollows the Reach has lost
topics.say: The roll of the burned grows with every hold that chooses fire. I keep every name in it.
fx: Thornwold's hanging glade: burned, and quiet now.
Fenmarch's drowned nave: burned, and quiet now.
Wardmoor's oath-stone: burned, and quiet now.
The Iron Downs' collapsed mine: burned, and quiet now.
Hollowbrook's barrow-court: burned, and quiet now.
The Saltkerns' drowned fleet: burned, and quiet now.

topics.label: Fenmarch, and Cinderhall's own
topics.say: Warders thrown off Stilt Row in Fenmarch. Aldous ruined in his own chapterhouse. Both reached me the same season. I do not forgive either quietly.

topics.label: the drains under the Lower Town
topics.say: Word reached me. Someone dealt with what was coming up under the Lower Town.
fx: 'Fire. Finally, someone in this city with sense.'
'Walled it up instead. Half a cure. At least it's quiet.'
'Words. The Church's answer, not mine — but it held, and I've seen fewer things hold than I'd like.'

topics.label: leave him to the roll
topics.say: Every name gets read. Even yours, in the end.

mg_mother.name: Mother Ysme
mg_mother.desc: Small, quick, ash to the wrists, unimpressed by everything including you.

topics.label: the Church in the capital
topics.say: Tolerated. The Regent lets us keep the rites the way you let a dog keep a bone: as long as it does not growl. We say the words over the burned anyway. Somebody should.

topics.label: the pilgrims' door
topics.say: Under the font. Keepers used it, when there were keepers, to go down and sit with what is under the palace.
fx: 'The Church knows what you did for it in the holds,' she says, and pulls the bolt herself.
She looks past you at Osk. 'You are one of ours,' she says to him, and pulls the bolt. 'See that this one deserves it.'
'And I would open it for a stranger why?' she says. 'Do the Church a kindness somewhere and come back.'

topics.label: Brother Osk
topics.say: A novice from the Vale chapel, with the fens in his face. Whatever you have done with him, do not make him watch a burning. Some of us do not come back from that.

topics.label: the drowned nave at Fenmarch
topics.say: The Prior wrote to me. The congregation sings no more at dusk, and the Priory admitted its part. That is a rite, whatever the Regent's roll calls it. The Church does not forget who held it.

topics.label: the rested holds, heard from afar
topics.say: Word from Barrowmere, word from Gullhaven — rites held properly, congregations settled. The Church in this city hears less good news than that most years.

topics.label: Brother Osk's own family
topics.say: Osk said the rite over his own family and did not stumble it, they tell me. Whatever novice he was when he left here, he is not that anymore.

topics.label: the true pardon read at Thornwold
topics.say: Forty years late, someone finally read a true pardon whole and named every man on it. That is a rite, whatever the Regent's roll calls it.

topics.label: the gathering under the drains
topics.say: Word reached the chapel of what was under the Lower Town.
fx: 'Rested,' she says, and for once looks like she believes her own rites work. 'That's more than I hoped from a stranger.'
'Walled in, not settled.' She doesn't hide her disappointment. 'A door shut on grief is still a door on grief.'
She's quiet a long moment. 'You didn't ask me first,' she says, 'and now there's nothing left to ask about.'

topics.label: leave her to the font
topics.say: Go carefully, and say the words even when nobody is listening.

mg_quill.name: Quill
mg_quill.desc: Small, neat, dealing cards to nobody.

topics.label: who you are
topics.say: Quill. I fix things for the Companies in the capital — passage, papers, the occasional absence. You have the look of someone who came over the pass without a writ. Or with one you did not earn.

topics.label: a way under the palace
topics.say: There is a cut from a cellar in the warrens down into the cistern. The Companies use it for barrels. It would carry a person.
fx: 'The Captain's word came over the pass ahead of you,' Quill says. 'Three knocks and a pause. The cellar is under the Gray Steps.'
'The Companies know your name kindly,' Quill says. 'Three knocks and a pause. Under the Gray Steps.'
Ten coins vanish under a card. 'Three knocks and a pause,' Quill says. 'Under the Gray Steps. We never spoke.'
'For strangers, ten coins,' Quill says. 'For friends of the Companies, a smile. You are neither yet.'

topics.label: a rider called Cal
topics.say: Sorrel Vane's company? Then he is in the Thornwold, or under it. The Companies do not send men to Marrowgate; Marrowgate sends for them, and they do not come back the same.

topics.label: what happened at Gullhaven
topics.say: Gullhaven's stair is ours now, thanks to you. Rennick still talks about it. That is the kind of debt the Companies actually pay back.

topics.label: word of Rook's toll at Thornwold
topics.say: Rook's toll on the Thornwold track — everyone in the trade heard how that went.
fx: Talked him straight into the Company proper. Vane still tells that one.
Paid him off clean. Rook respects coin more than most respect people.
Put him down instead. The toll's gone quiet, one way or another.

topics.label: a robbed grave, a hatch under the pass
topics.say: A bribed grave-robber in Hollowbrook, a hatch under the Coldpass brazier — small trades, but the Companies remember who is good for them.

topics.label: a purse for the Lower Town guilds
topics.say: 'The Companies want the guilds' voice on the market steps, and voices cost coin.' He slides a purse across. 'Ropewalk loft, west of the shed. Don't lose it to the drains.'

topics.label: what became of the Companies' coin
topics.say: That purse of mine — word of it came back to me, one way or another.
fx: 'Landed clean,' he says. 'The Companies don't forget an honest courier.'
'Tarn's men came asking about a purse. I don't know what you told them, and I'd rather not.'
'A purse light by exactly what it should weigh doesn't go unnoticed forever,' he says. 'My cut on anything you need from me just went up.'

topics.label: sell him the burn-order
topics.say: 'Now that,' Quill says, eyeing the burn-order, 'is worth something to the right buyer.'
fx: Coin changes hands, and the burn-order changes pockets. 'The Ironbound's own hand on it,' he says, pleased. 'We'll find a use.'

topics.label: leave Quill to the cards
topics.say: Three knocks and a pause. Everything is three knocks and a pause.

mg_archivist.name: Archivist Penn
mg_archivist.desc: Ink to the second knuckle and a candle held like a weapon.

topics.label: the Hall of Ledgers
topics.say: Every tithe, every hanging, every harvest since the founding. Nothing in this hall is secret. Some of it is chained, which is a different thing.

topics.label: the chained shelf
topics.say: The founding ledger. The first Reeve wrote it himself and chained it himself. Every Regent since has read it and left the chain on.
fx: 'Mother Ysme says you are to be trusted with the dead,' Penn says, and takes a key from around his neck. The chain drops.
Penn looks at the coins for a long moment and then at the chain. 'I am paid in candles,' he says, and takes the key from his neck.
'It can be read by the Regent, the Church's Mother, or someone with fifteen gold and no shame,' Penn says. 'Or by a thief. I would know which you were.'

topics.label: the key to the barred stair
topics.say: The stair goes down to what the palace stands on. I have the key because nobody else would carry it.
fx: 'You have read what is down there,' Penn says. 'Then you may as well see it.' The key is warm from his neck.
Penn listens to you for longer than he meant to. 'Four hundred years,' he says, 'and nobody has asked me for it politely.' The key is warm from his neck.
'No,' Penn says, and goes back to his shelves.

topics.label: the exile line
topics.say: So one of them is alive, and travelling with you. The ledger says the exile line was to be struck off. The ledger says many things. I have never once struck a name off anything.

topics.label: what Hollowbrook's Keepers found
topics.say: The Keepers' Hall found what we chained here — an exile's name struck from a Marrowgate line. Properly kept, properly found. I almost envy their shelf.

topics.label: the Wardmoor record, given or taken
topics.say: Highward's sealed shelf, opened one way or another. I heard which.
fx: Asked for honestly, and given. That is how a record ought to leave a shelf.
Taken without asking. I keep every ledger I can precisely so that does not happen.

topics.label: Hollowbrook's mounds, sold to the Crown
topics.say: Every mound the surveyor mapped is a grave I will never get to read properly before someone digs it for its rings. I keep the ledgers. I do not have to like what fills them.

topics.label: the Tanners' Row proof
topics.say: Whatever you did with what turned up, casks or ledgers, it came from a shelf or a cellar I could have shown you myself.
fx: 'Told the Marshal outright. Good. A record means nothing kept quiet.'
'Given to the Regent. I won't ask what she did with it. I can guess.'
'Sold to the Free Companies. Of all the shelves that could have held it, that's the one I never chained.'

topics.label: leave Penn to his candle
topics.say: Mind the shelves. They are the only honest thing in this palace.

mg_first_reeve.name: the first Reeve's shade
mg_first_reeve.desc: Grief made a man, or the other way round.

topics.label: who you were
topics.say: Reeve of the Vale, once. Then a thief. Then a founder. They built me a king's tomb and I have sat on the lid of it every night since, because I cannot lie down in what I did.

topics.label: your father rests
topics.say: He — rests? Without the crown, or with it? It does not matter. Then hear it, because I have said it to no one: I took it from his brow while he slept, and called it inheritance, and the Vale ate that winter.
fx: The gray coming off him thins to a thread.

topics.label: speak the keepers' words to him
topics.say: The keepers. I had them struck off, every one. And still one came down each year and sat with me and said those words, and I could not answer. I can now: I took it from his brow while he slept, and called it inheritance.
fx: The gray coming off him thins to a thread.

topics.label: show him his own ledger
topics.say: My hand. I wrote it the night after and chained it the morning after that, so that someone would read it and no one would. You read it. Then it is said: I took it from his brow while he slept, and called it inheritance.
fx: The gray coming off him thins to a thread.

topics.label: your father is dust
topics.say: Dust. Then I am the last of it, and there is nothing left to say it to. Do what you came to do. The seat is through there.

topics.label: the Hollow Throne
topics.say: I cut it hollow for his crown — a gift I never gave. All the Reach's grief pours from it. Fill it: three holds rested, my father at rest, my confession. Burn it: Ironbound oil. Sit: a crown. Or read my ledger aloud.

topics.label: how many hollows burned
topics.say: Three hollows or more, gone to fire while I sat this lid. Perhaps that is a mercy too. I have run out of certainty about which acts are which.

topics.label: how many hollows rest
topics.say: Five hollows resting easy, and only the one under me still restless. I begin to think you might actually finish what I could not.

topics.label: leave him on the lid
topics.say: Go on. I have heard every footstep for four hundred years. Yours is not the last.

mg_gate_guard.name: gate captain
mg_gate_guard.desc: Enamelled gray and a face that has said no for a living.
onDeath: The captain goes down on the white steps. The bronze doors are only doors now. Behind you the Way has emptied, and someone is running for the Watch House.

mg_hollow_guard.name: honour guard
onDeath: The gray mail folds down on nothing. Four hundred years at a post, ended by whoever came next.

mg_cutpurse.name: cutpurse
onDeath: The boy drops the knife and three coins that were not his either, and is gone into the washing before he hits the ground.

topics.label: what you watch for
topics.say: The gray comes up the drains at the third bell; every night a step farther. Under the chapel there is a stair the keepers used; under the Gray Steps a cellar the Companies use. Both go down. Everything here goes down.

topics.label: give him a coin
topics.say: He takes it without looking at it. 'The Regent's face,' he says. 'Her grandfather's on the old ones. Same face. Same hollow behind it.'

stages.text: You stand before the Hollow Throne. Fill it, burn it, sit in it, or read the truth aloud — each is an ending.
The first Reeve has confessed. The Hollow Throne lies north of his tomb.
The honour guard is passed. The first Reeve's tomb lies north through the crypts; hear him before the throne.
The barred stair is open. Down, through the cistern, north into the old crypts.
The pilgrims' door under the Chapel of Ash leads down to the cistern; the crypts lie north of it.
Quill's cut: under the Gray Steps in the warrens, three knocks and a pause, down to the cistern.
You are inside the palace. The archivist keeps the key to the barred stair; the Regent keeps her window.
A seat under the palace takes a rite, fire, a crown, or the truth read aloud. Ways down: stair, chapel, Quill's cut.
The chained shelf in the Hall of Ledgers, east of the palace court. Penn, the Church, gold, or your own hands.
The founding ledger is chained in the palace's Hall of Ledgers. It would prove what the House of Ashreeve stands on.

epilogue.text: Ysolde Ashreeve kept the founding ledger on her own table after that, unchained, where anyone who came to her could read it.
In Marrowgate they still argue whether the Regent's killing was justice. The argument is the closest thing the city has to a rite.
Regent Vell rules the Reach from the Hollow Throne, precisely and without mercy, and has never once spoken your name.
Nothing stands in the old crypts now. The Watch goes down with lamps on feast days and finds only water.
The gate captain's name is on the Watch's roll of honour. Yours is on a different roll, in the same hall.
All six hollows rest now — not one hold in the Reach still grieves by fire or by neglect.
Three holds or more went to the torch. The Ironbound call it mercy. Not everyone agrees.
He confessed, four hundred years late — and the throne burned anyway. Some call that the cruelest mercy of all.

stamps.landmark: a lit cell across the water
